title: Normalization of a prescribed rational simple-root pinning
statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple rational Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra], [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra]. Fix a maximal abelian subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ acting diagonally, and its reduced root system $R\subset\mathfrak h^\vee$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in R}\mathfrak g_\alpha$ with one-dimensional root spaces $\mathfrak g_\alpha=\{x:[h,x]=\alpha(h)x\text{ for all }h\}$. Let $h_\alpha\in\mathfrak h$ be the coroot, characterized by $h_\alpha\in[\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}]$ and $\alpha(h_\alpha)=2$. Fix a simple-root base $\Delta$ (a basis of $\mathfrak h^\vee$ with sign-coherent integer coordinates for all roots) and arbitrary nonzero rational $x_\delta\in\mathfrak g_\delta$ for $\delta\in\Delta$. These prescribed vectors extend to nonzero rational $e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ for all roots, with $e_\delta=x_\delta$, such that $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$. If $\alpha+\beta\in R$, then $$[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=\varepsilon_{\alpha,\beta}(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)e_{\alpha+\beta},\qquad \varepsilon_{\alpha,\beta}\in\{1,-1\},$$ where $p_{\alpha,\beta}=\max\{p\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}:\beta-p\alpha\in R\}$. If $\alpha+\beta\notin R\cup\{0\}$ the bracket is zero. Thus the $h_\delta,e_\alpha$ form a rational basis, called a Chevalley basis, with integer structure constants. The empty base is allowed.

source.place: Section 23h, Chevalley bases, printed pp.508--509, especially Theorem 23.71; extending the prescribed simple-root pinning, with rationality from bracket construction over the split rational form.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans] to the evaluation pairing $\mathfrak h^\vee\times\mathfrak h\to\mathbf Q$ and the given root-coroot system. It gives a basis $(h_\delta)_{\delta\in\Delta}$ of $\mathfrak h$, integral expressions for every coroot in that basis, and the nonnegative-coroot clause required to package $\Delta$ as a Mathlib root-pairing base. The root-side base hypotheses are exactly those of the item. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-opposition-involution] to obtain a rational involution $\theta$ with $\theta|_{\mathfrak h}=-1$ and $[x_\delta,-\theta(x_\delta)]=h_\delta$.

source.place: Appendix C.21--C.26, pp.612--613; Section 23h, p.508, normalized simple-root triples and opposition.

proof.text: For a root $\alpha$, let $Q(\alpha)$ mean that there exists a rational $z\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ with $[z,-\theta(z)]=h_\alpha$. This implies $z\ne0$ since $\alpha(h_\alpha)=2$. The simple-root case is $z=x_\delta$. If $Q(\alpha)$ holds, take $-\theta(z)$ for $-\alpha$: its bracket with its negative $\theta$-image is $[-\theta(z),z]=-h_\alpha=h_{-\alpha}$. Here $h_{-\alpha}=-h_\alpha$ follows from the defining coroot characterization. For the additive step, suppose $\gamma=\alpha+\delta\in R$ and $\delta\in\Delta$, and choose $z$ witnessing $Q(\alpha)$. Put $p=\max\{n\geq0:\delta-n\alpha\in R\}$. By [lem-sfb-opposition-root-bracket-norm], $w=[z,x_\delta]$ satisfies $[w,-\theta(w)]=(p+1)^2h_\gamma$. Thus $w/(p+1)$ witnesses $Q(\gamma)$; $p+1\ne0$ in $\mathbf Q$. The bracket has weight $\gamma$ by Jacobi. The base, negative and additive clauses of [lem-sfb-root-base-additive-induction] now prove $Q$ for every root.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.508--509, opposition and Theorem 23.71; agent rational induction replacing complex normalizations.

proof.text: For each positive root choose a witness to $Q$, retaining $e_\delta=x_\delta$ at the simple roots, and define $e_{-\alpha}=-\theta(e_\alpha)$. The sign-coherent base coordinates partition the roots into positive and negative ones, so these choices assign exactly one vector to every root. They are nonzero and rational, and satisfy $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$ in both signs and $e_{-\alpha}=-\theta(e_\alpha)$. This is just the preceding existence claim and skew-symmetry.

source.place: Section 23h, p.508, extending the simple-root pinning; agent rational choice of the normalized vectors.

proof.text: If $\gamma=\alpha+\beta\in R$, Jacobi gives $[h,[e_\alpha,e_\beta]]=\gamma(h)[e_\alpha,e_\beta]$ for all $h\in\mathfrak h$. The one-dimensional rational root space therefore gives $[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=N e_\gamma$ with $N\in\mathbf Q$. Apply [lem-sfb-opposition-root-bracket-norm] to $e_\alpha,e_\beta$. Rational linearity of $\theta$ and normalization give $N^2h_\gamma=(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)^2h_\gamma$. Since $\gamma(h_\gamma)=2$, cancellation yields $N^2=(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)^2$. Factoring over $\mathbf Q$ gives $N=\pm(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)$.

If $\alpha+\beta\notin R\cup\{0\}$, the same Jacobi identity makes the bracket a vector of the nonexistent nonzero weight $\alpha+\beta$, hence it is zero by the stated root decomposition. The vectors $e_\alpha$ are bases of their individual root spaces, so together with the simple coroot basis from [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans] they form a rational basis of $\mathfrak g$. The remaining products are $[h_\delta,h_\epsilon]=0$ and $[h_\delta,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h_\delta)e_\alpha$ with integral coefficient by crystallographicity. Opposite-root products are coroots, whose simple-coroot coordinates are integral by that same cited node. Thus every structure constant is integral. If $\Delta=\varnothing$, its being a basis gives $\mathfrak h=0$, whence $R=\varnothing$ and the given decomposition gives $\mathfrak g=0$; the empty basis proves the assertion.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.508--509, bracket table and integral Lie lattice; Appendix C.26, p.613.

proof_origin.place: Section 23h, pp.508--509: rational construction by additive root induction using opposition and the local squared bracket identity; Appendix C.21--C.26 for bases.
